items.action: Update Content Scanner Tools to ≥ 25.3.0.5525 on all SEG appliances with File Reputation enabled; review Cisco's IOCs. Managed-cloud customers contacted by Cisco should engage with Cisco remediation.
items.details: Found via Cisco's internal scanning; exploitation confirmed in October 2026. Affects SEG where File Reputation is enabled and Content Scanner Tools < 25.3.0.5525. Cisco published IOCs and contacted managed Secure Email Cloud customers showing compromise indicators.
items.summary: Cisco disclosed on Oct 14 that attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-76519 (CVSS 9.8) in Secure Email Gateway: a path traversal in the AMP File Reputation feature lets an unauthenticated attacker send a crafted attachment that writes files and executes commands as root — no login or user interaction needed.
items.title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway zero-day under active exploitation

items.action: Patch to 25.1.3.0/25.1.3.1, 22.8R2.5, or 25.1.1.2; run memory + network forensics (not just the Integrity Checker); on suspected compromise, follow Ivanti's recovery procedure — assume compromise, factory-reset, and rotate every credential and certificate.
items.details: CISA added it to the KEV catalog on Oct 13 with an Oct 16 federal deadline; used for credential theft and data exfiltration. Affects 25.1.1.1 and earlier, 25.1.2.2 and earlier, 22.8R2.4 and earlier. The third (privilege-escalation) flaw is still unpatched.
items.summary: Ivanti pushed emergency patches for CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass allowing unauthenticated remote command execution on Connect Secure. Volexity attributes exploitation to a new group, UTA0576, which chained three zero-days entirely in memory — so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool cannot detect the compromise.
items.title: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day chained by UTA0576 — KEV-listed, federal deadline Oct 16

items.action: Patch CVE-2026-96951 first (before Oct 16), then work through the 78 critical fixes prioritizing internet-facing systems; update .NET Framework where WDAC is enforced.
items.details: Two more zero-days were publicly disclosed before patching: CVE-2026-108398 (.NET Framework WDAC bypass, found by Google Project Zero's James Forshaw) and CVE-2026-92707 (MessagePack-CSharp DoS) — neither confirmed exploited yet.
items.summary: Microsoft's October Patch Tuesday (Oct 14) fixes 1,414 vulnerabilities including 78 critical. The priority item is CVE-2026-96951 (CVSS 8.8), an actively exploited Windows Shell command-injection flaw that bypasses Mark of the Web protections (SmartScreen/Protected View); CISA KEV-listed it on Oct 13 with an Oct 16 federal deadline.
items.title: Microsoft October Patch Tuesday: 1,414 flaws, one exploited zero-day

items.action: Nextcloud admins: update richdocumentscode to ≥ 26.4.303 or remove the app entirely; hunt for web shells, especially on servers restarted since early September.
items.details: Disabling the app does NOT mitigate — it must be updated to 26.4.303 or removed. The fixed version shipped Sep 11 but the advisory only came Oct 14, leaving a disclosure gap.
items.summary: Collabora published an Oct 14 advisory for CVE-2026-110447 in its 'Collabora Online – Built-in CODE Server' Nextcloud app: an unauthenticated request can execute commands on the server when the local document server isn't running (restart/upgrade/crash). Attackers have been planting web shells since Sep 10.
items.title: Nextcloud servers backdoored via critical Collabora CODE app flaw

items.details: The count was revised upward from 183 after two external security firms investigated. The bank blocked the attacker IPs, deployed emergency verification logic, is notifying affected customers individually, and reported to South Korea's Financial Supervisory Service.
items.summary: South Korea's OK Savings Bank confirmed on Oct 15 that a hacking attack on its online loan application service (Oct 11, 8:44 PM – Oct 12, 2:14 AM) exposed personal and financial data of 250 customers — names, birth dates, mobile numbers, account numbers, addresses, annual income, and loan amounts.
items.title: OK Savings Bank confirms breach: 250 customers' data exposed

items.details: The claim is unverified (from the actor's own listing, indexed on ransomware.live). If genuine, the group says client-site surveillance feeds are 'dark until settlement' — a supply-chain risk for all of Interior Technologies' customers.
items.summary: Emerging ransomware group N0n listed California-based Interior Technologies on its leak site on Oct 14, marking the entry 'NOT PAID — EXPOSED' and claiming to have taken the company's complete gateway configuration — every client site, device, user, and credential.
items.title: N0n ransomware claims breach of smart-building integrator Interior Technologies

items.details: The claim is unverified; no entry vector or exfiltration extent disclosed. The healthcare/pharma angle makes it the more impactful of the day's pharma/manufacturing claims.
items.summary: On Oct 14, the Eclipse ransomware group claimed Taiwan Otsuka Pharmaceutical (founded 1974) as a victim. Supporting infostealer exposure data cites 162 exposed passwords tied to the victim's domain — including two marked critical — suggesting an infostealer-led foothold.
items.title: Eclipse ransomware claims Taiwan Otsuka Pharmaceutical

items.details: The claim is unverified; ransomware.live shows the listing with a note about the firm's complete business email archive. Qilin is an established group, which raises the claim's relative credibility.
items.summary: On Oct 14, Qilin listed U.S. architecture firm MOA Architecture (moaarch.com) on its leak site, with the victim domain showing 137 exposed passwords — two classified critical — and Microsoft 365 usage.
items.title: Qilin lists U.S. architecture firm MOA Architecture on its leak site

items.details: Funds moved via IMPS/NEFT to mule accounts with dummy reference identifiers and amounts exceeding per-transaction limits; a Chennai-developed platform with deficient payout-API controls was allegedly the initial foothold. CERT-In advised suspending compromised APIs, rotating credentials, MFA, and maker-checker approvals.
items.summary: CERT-In (with CSIRT-Fin) issued advisory CIAD-2026-0046 warning of coordinated campaigns stealing payment aggregator/gateway and partner-bank API credentials to trigger unauthorised fund transfers from within victims' own whitelisted infrastructure — bypassing KYC, loan-sanction, beneficiary-verification, and transaction-limit controls. ET reports up to 20 financial institutions were affected.
items.title: CERT-In warns: API-hijacking campaign hit ~20 financial institutions

items.details: Dubai-based handlers supplied an app called 'Banker Panel' that split stolen funds across thousands of mule accounts in one click, defeating banks' 'golden hour' freeze window. Seizures: 15 laptops, 128 ATM cards, 85 phones, 76 SIM cards; ~₹120 crore frozen across 7,500 accounts. Funds went onward to Dubai via the informal 'angadia' courier network.
items.summary: The Mumbai Police Crime Branch uncovered two fraud networks operating out of luxury villas in Goa, arresting 22 men. Police estimate ~₹900 crore was routed through thousands of mule accounts linked to 186 cybercrime cases.
items.title: Mumbai Police bust ₹900-crore cyber-fraud laundering network

items.details: In the Mumbai case, the scam began Sep 19 and escalated through fake ATS/IPS personas with continuous video surveillance. Separately, Maharashtra Cyber Cell rescued two elderly women mid-scam — one in Sambhaji Nagar defrauded of ₹27 lakh of a demanded ₹3 crore — using real-time transaction tracing of a Layer-1 mule account.
items.summary: On Oct 14, multiple high-value 'digital arrest' scams surfaced: a 74-year-old businessman and his 77-year-old wife from Peddar Road, Mumbai, lost ₹4.52 crore to fraudsters impersonating Mumbai Police, ATS, NIA, Supreme Court, and RBI officials; a 72-year-old woman in Hyderabad lost ₹2.2 crore to a fake-CBI caller, prompting a fresh police advisory.
items.title: Digital-arrest scams surge: elderly lose crores in Mumbai and Hyderabad
